claims.text: Limb (d) of POL-NS-01 fails on the face of the trip record, so the baseline charge never gets off the ground. The trip was terminated by the driver with cancellation_reason_code DRIVER_UNABLE_TO_LOCATE, which is not one of the three codes the clause recognises (RIDER_NO_SHOW, RIDER_UNREACHABLE, EXCESSIVE_WAIT). The clause is explicit that DRIVER_UNABLE_TO_LOCATE is the driver's own admission that he could not find the rider, does not satisfy limb (d), and sends the trip to POL-NS-03. With limb (d) broken, the $4.00 is not chargeable under POL-NS-01 at all.

The GPS arrival test fails as well. The driver's trace carries 92 fixes across the whole 15 minute window and not one of them is a qualifying fix inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius: derived.arrival.qualifying_fix_count is 0, and the driver's closest approach over the entire trace is 259.94 m from the Blk 118 pin. Under POL-NS-02 no qualifying in-radius fix exists in the 15 minutes preceding the cancellation, so the driver never arrived, POL-NS-01 limb (b) fails, and the rider is entitled to a full refund of the cancellation fee.

Dwell shortfall, stated in numbers as POL-NS-06 requires: the required minimum for STANDARD is 300 seconds and the effective in-geofence dwell is 0 seconds (longest_qualifying_run.duration_sec 0, run_count 0, shortfall 300 seconds). A dwell of zero against a 300 second minimum means the fee is not chargeable and is refunded to the rider in full, whether or not the rider was present and whether or not she responded to messages.

Disclosure: EV-ADVIS-00205-01 is MISSING with weight 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, and I cite it for its absence. No advisory covers Rivervale Drive in this window, so POL-NS-06(i) cannot be run in the driver's favour: limb (i) permits separate in-geofence intervals to be summed only where a traffic_advisory is present and populated with a kerb-restriction, enforcement, closure or accident type, and the clause itself says a MISSING advisory makes the limb unavailable. The 300 second shortfall therefore stands unmodified.

Even on the reading most favourable to the driver — that he held position for the required dwell at some point outside the 50 m radius but inside the 400 m ceiling, his closest approach for the whole trip being 259.94 m — POL-NS-03 does not save the fee. On those facts the driver still did not arrive at the pickup point, POL-NS-01 limb (b) still fails, and POL-NS-03 refunds the cancellation fee to the rider in full. The only thing POL-NS-03 leaves open is the driver's compensation, and that is resolved against him below.

The pin-ambiguity escape is closed on this trip. POL-NS-03(ii) attributes a mislocation to pin ambiguity rather than to a party only where trip_record.registered_pickup_points is 2 or more; this trip records exactly 1 registered pickup point at the Blk 118 pin, so there is no platform-funded goodwill to allocate and no basis for calling this an ambiguous pin rather than a driver who stopped at the wrong block.

Fault under POL-NS-03(i) runs against the driver. The rider named the block in chat — 'im at blk 118, the one facing the carpark' — and the driver read that message at 07:22:30 and answered 'ok coming' at 07:22:48, so this is not a message he never saw. He nonetheless never moved to Blk 118: his closest approach in the entire trace is 259.94 m from that pin, and he cancelled at 07:33:05 without ever entering the arrival radius. A driver who is told the correct block, acknowledges it, and does not move to it before cancelling bears the loss and receives no compensation. Disclosure: the chat log EV-CHAT-00205 is IMPAIRED at weight 0.8 with issue code CONTENT_REDACTED; the redaction removed only the unit number, and the operative identifier 'blk 118' survives intact, so this claim survives the discount.

POL-NS-04 independently exonerates the rider. Limb (a): she sent a locating message during the waiting window, 'i dont see you at 118 leh' at 07:29:15, stating that she could not see the vehicle. Limb (b): the driver posted no reply to that message and trip_record.in_app_calls is empty, so no reply and no call came within 120 seconds of it or at all before he terminated the trip at 07:33:05; his earlier 'ok coming' answered the 07:22:10 message three minutes before he claimed to have arrived, not the locating message left hanging while he stood where she could not see him. Limb (c): the rider track is clean and places her device 96 qualifying fixes out of 96 with a maximum distance of 22.79 m from the pin, far inside the 100 m STANDARD rider-presence radius. Disclosure: EV-CHAT-00205 is IMPAIRED at weight 0.8 with issue code CONTENT_REDACTED, which does not touch the message text or timestamps this limb turns on. On POL-NS-04 the fee is refunded in full with no driver compensation payable.

This case is decidable on this record and no escalation limb is engaged on the profiles. rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 1, well below the 3 that POL-NS-09(d) reads, and the POL-NS-07 anti-farming check does not trip: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 2 against 104 completed trips, so neither the count limb nor the rate limb is met (2 is below 4, and 0.019 is far under 0.08). Both counterparts' disputes_with_counterparty_90d are 0. There is no basis to hold this fee away from the rider pending review.

On the remedy: this dispute was filed by the rider, the $4.00 cancellation fee is shown as CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.00, and the amount reconciles with the fee schedule — STANDARD zone fee 4.00 against RYDE_X vehicle tier fee 4.00, the greater of the two being 4.00, so the charge line itself is not in dispute as to quantum. A ruling on POL-NS-01, POL-NS-02, POL-NS-03, POL-NS-04 or POL-NS-06 returns the whole of that $4.00 to the filing party as a FULL_REFUND, with amount_sgd of 4.00.

claims.text: The rider cannot run this dispute through POL-NS-04, because limb (b) fails on the chat log's own timestamps. Limb (a) is met — the rider's 07:22:10 message names his block — but the driver sent MSG-00205-002 ('ok coming') at 07:22:48, 38 seconds later and far inside the 120 second window, so no finding of unanswered rider contact can be entered against the driver and limb (c) is never reached. Disclosure of impairment, as POL-GEN-02(1) requires: EV-CHAT-00205 carries weight_multiplier 0.8 on issue CONTENT_REDACTED (the unit number in MSG-00205-001 was redacted). The redaction removes no timestamp and no sender, so the 38 second interval this claim rests on is untouched by the discount.

The 4.00 fee cannot be carried by POL-NS-01, and the driver does not pretend otherwise. Limb (d) is excluded by the clause's own text because the trip terminated with cancellation_reason_code DRIVER_UNABLE_TO_LOCATE; limb (b) fails because the driver's nearest approach to the pickup pin is 259.94 m against a 50 m STANDARD arrival radius; and limb (c) fails because the qualifying in-radius fix count is zero out of 92 driver fixes, leaving no in-geofence dwell to set against the 300 second minimum. This is exactly the case POL-NS-01 hands to POL-NS-03 — the category's clause for an honest mislocation rather than a manufactured no-show — and the dispute is to be reasoned there, not on the baseline clause.

What the record does establish is an honest wrong-block attempt, and that distinction should be written into the ruling. The trip record computes a wait_time_min of 6.4 running from the arrived event at 07:26:40 to the cancellation at 07:33:05: the driver gave the rider six and a half minutes rather than harvesting a fee. His closest approach to the pin is 259.94 m — inside POL-NS-03's 400 m wrong-entrance ceiling and inside POL-NS-05's 300 m line. POL-NS-05 catches only an arrival fix that puts the driver more than 300 m out, or in motion at 15 kph or above, at the arrived timestamp; the published derived facts key no distance and no speed to that timestamp, and the only distance they publish sits inside the 300 m line, so the false-marker limb is not made out. This trip therefore belongs to the wrong-entrance route POL-NS-05's closing sentence preserves, and it should not be recorded as a false-arrival event against the driver.

Two points are closed against the driver on this record and the driver does not stretch them. First, the pin-ambiguity limb of POL-NS-03(ii) requires trip_record.registered_pickup_points of 2 or more; this trip records one registered pickup point, so the platform-funded goodwill of 50 per cent — 2.00 against the 4.00 fee — is unavailable and the derived goodwill figure has nothing to attach to. Second, the rider did name the block, MSG-00205-001 reading 'im at blk 118', with the redaction removing only the unit number, so under POL-NS-03(i) the residual loss sits with the driver and no compensation is payable to him. The chat artifact is impaired at weight 0.8 on issue CONTENT_REDACTED, which is why the surviving block identifier, and not the redacted unit number, is the fact relied on.

The sum charged is not open to attack on integrity grounds, and no partial refund can be built on it. The fare breakdown carries a single cancellation-fee line of 4.00 SGD, and 4.00 is exactly the greater of the two schedule figures this trip attracts — the STANDARD zone-class fee of 4.00 and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee of 4.00, the schedule dimension resolving to a tie — so the line reconciles with fee_schedule.resolution_rule and no limb of POL-NS-08(d) is engaged on this trip.

There is no fee-farming pattern behind this cancelled trip. On the two fields POL-NS-07 names, and no others, driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 2, below the 4 the clause requires, and 2 over driver_profile.completed_trips_30d of 104 is a rate of 0.019, below the 0.08 the clause also requires: the anti-farming test fails on both limbs, so nothing on the driver's 30-day record supports an adverse inference. On the rider side, rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 1 against POL-NS-09(d)'s threshold of 3, and the counterparty-dispute counts are 0 and 0 against POL-NS-09(c)'s threshold of 2. Under POL-GEN-01 every other entry on either profile — rating, acceptance rate, lifetime counters — is context only and can ground nothing.

In the alternative, and only if the Judge is not prepared to run the wrong-entrance findings, this case should be escalated rather than guessed at. The trip record and the trace contradict each other directly on arrival and dwell: the record enters an arrived event at 07:26:40 with a 6.4 minute wait, while the 92 driver fixes never come closer to the pin than 259.94 m and show zero in-geofence dwell. The published derived facts key neither a distance nor a speed to the arrived timestamp, so POL-NS-05 cannot be run (its condition needs a fix more than 300 m out or at 15 kph at that timestamp) and POL-NS-03 cannot be run either (its condition needs a stationary hold within 400 m). That head-on conflict between two admissible artifacts is what POL-NS-09(b) exists for, and under POL-GEN-03 the consequence is a terminal escalation with the disputed 4.00 held rather than refunded.

ruling.explanation:
Rider and driver, here is the decision. The $4.00 cancellation fee is refunded to the rider in full, and no compensation is payable to the driver.

The fee cannot be charged. POL-NS-01 requires all four conditions to hold and three of them fail. (b) Arrival: across the whole 15-minute window the driver's 92 GPS fixes contain zero qualifying fixes within the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius at the Blk 118 pin, and his closest approach was 259.94 m, so the POL-NS-02 arrival test is not met. (c) Dwell: the effective in-geofence dwell is 0 seconds against the 300-second STANDARD minimum, a 300-second shortfall, so POL-NS-06 refunds the fee on the arithmetic alone. (d) Reason code: the trip ended with DRIVER_UNABLE_TO_LOCATE, which is not one of the three codes the clause recognises and is the driver's own statement that he could not find the rider. Any one of these defeats the charge.

POL-NS-03 is the clause this trip belongs to, and it also refunds the fee in full: the driver held position outside the arrival radius but inside the 400 m ceiling (nearest approach 259.94 m), so he did not arrive at the pickup point.

Fault and the driver's compensation. POL-NS-03 decides fault from the chat log. The rider named the correct block — 'im at blk 118, the one facing the carpark' at 07:22:10 — the driver read it at 07:22:30 and replied 'ok coming' at 07:22:48, and he never moved to Blk 118 before cancelling at 07:33:05. Under POL-NS-03(i) the driver bears the loss and receives nothing. The pin-ambiguity goodwill of POL-NS-03(ii) is unavailable: this trip has one registered pickup point, not the two or more that limb requires, so no platform-funded 50% payment arises. The traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00205-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0), so POL-NS-06(i) cannot be used to accumulate dwell in the driver's favour, and POL-NS-07 does not apply because POL-NS-01 is not satisfied and POL-NS-03 displaces it.

POL-NS-04 does not need to be reached, and it changes nothing. The driver answered the rider's first locating message inside 120 seconds (38 seconds), so limb (b) is contested for that message; on any reading the fee is refunded in full under POL-NS-01, POL-NS-02, POL-NS-03 or POL-NS-06, with the same nil compensation either way.

Impairment and confidence. The chat log EV-CHAT-00205 is impaired at weight 0.8 on issue code CONTENT_REDACTED — the unit number in the rider's first message was redacted. It is NOT impaired for policy purposes: POL-NS-08(c) is not engaged, because the log holds all four messages the trip record counts and has no sequence gap or hole across the arrival marker. The finding it carries survives the discount, because the operative identifier, 'blk 118', is intact and only the unit number was removed. The arrival failure rests on the GPS trace and the trip record, both at weight 1.0; the fault allocation that fixes the driver's compensation at nil rests on the chat log at 0.8, so confidence is capped at 0.8. That is above the 0.70 escalation floor.

No escalation and no referral. The trip record's 'arrived' marker and the GPS trace are not a POL-NS-09(b) conflict: POL-NS-05 and POL-NS-03 are the clauses that decide what an arrival marker means, and the marker here resolves as an honest wrong-entrance hold under POL-NS-03. The profile and anti-farming limbs of POL-NS-09 do not fire (rider no-show disputes 1, below 3; driver no-show terminations 2 against 104 completed trips, below both the count and the rate threshold; counterparty disputes 0 and 0). No POL-NS-05(ii) false-arrival referral is made: no distance or speed is keyed to the arrived timestamp, and the driver's nearest approach (259.94 m) sits inside the clause's 300 m line.

ruling.explanation:
The $4.00 cancellation fee is refunded to the rider in full, and the driver receives no compensation.

Under POL-NS-01 a no-show fee needs all four conditions and three of them fail on this record. The driver's own cancellation code was DRIVER_UNABLE_TO_LOCATE, which is not one of the three codes the clause recognises, so limb (d) fails by the clause's own words. The trace carries 92 driver fixes and not one is a qualifying fix inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius; the driver's closest approach all trip was 259.94 m from the Blk 118 pin, so limb (b) fails. And with no in-geofence fix there is no in-geofence dwell at all — 0 seconds against the 300 second minimum — so limb (c) fails. Under POL-NS-02 the driver never arrived and the fee is refunded in full.

What the record shows is the wrong-block case POL-NS-03 governs. The driver did stop inside the 400 m ceiling — nearest approach 259.94 m — but at the wrong block, not at the pickup point, so POL-NS-03 refunds the fee to the rider in full. It then asks who bears the loss, and the chat answers: the rider sent 'im at blk 118, the one facing the carpark' at 07:22:10, the driver read it at 07:22:30 and replied 'ok coming' at 07:22:48, then never moved to Blk 118 before cancelling at 07:33:05. Under POL-NS-03(i) the driver bears the loss and gets nothing. The platform-funded pin-ambiguity goodwill in POL-NS-03(ii) is unavailable in any event: it needs 2 or more registered pickup points and this trip records exactly 1.

POL-NS-06 reaches the same answer independently — 0 seconds of the required 300 — so the fee is not chargeable. The only thing that could have altered that arithmetic, the traffic-advisory qualification in POL-NS-06(i), has nothing behind it: EV-ADVIS-00205-01 is MISSING with weight 0.0 and issue MISSING_ARTIFACT, so the 300 second shortfall stands unmodified.

On POL-NS-04, the driver's objection is noted: limb (b) can be read so that the 38 second reply to the 07:22:10 message answers the rider's contact. Even on that reading the refund does not depend on POL-NS-04, because POL-NS-02, POL-NS-03 and POL-NS-06 each require it. The rider's own track puts her within 22.8 m of the pin on all 96 of her fixes, inside the 100 m STANDARD rider-presence radius, and her 07:29:15 message 'i dont see you at 118 leh' drew no reply and no in-app call before the driver cancelled.

Weight and confidence. EV-CHAT-00205 carries the POL-NS-03(i) fault allocation and is impaired at weight 0.8 on issue CONTENT_REDACTED; the redaction took only the unit number, the block identifier 'blk 118' survives, and the allocation turns on nothing the redaction removed, so the finding survives the discount. That artifact sets the cap at 0.8. The money facts — non-arrival, the zero dwell, and the $4.00 amount — come from the GPS trace, trip record and fare breakdown, each at weight 1.0.

Nothing here escalates. The POL-NS-07 anti-farming check fails on both limbs (2 no-show terminations in 30 days against the 4 required; 2 over 104 completed trips, a rate of 0.019 against the 0.08 required). The rider's no_show_disputes_30d is 1 against POL-NS-09(d)'s threshold of 3, and the counterparty-dispute counts POL-NS-09(c) reads are 0 and 0. ruling.explanation:

Limb (d) fails: DRIVER_UNABLE_TO_LOCATE is expressly not one of the three codes the clause recognises, and the clause itself calls it the driver's own admission that he could not find the rider. POL-NS-02 therefore gives the rider a full refund, and POL-NS-06 reaches the same result on the dwell arithmetic. The fare line itself is sound — the greater of the STANDARD zone fee ($4.00) and the RYDE_X tier fee ($4.00) is $4.00, so no POL-NS-08(d) integrity defect — but no charge survives.

The wrong-entrance route (the driver's POL-NS-03/POL-NS-05 claim, accepted as far as it goes) arrives at the same place. Treating the driver as having held position outside the 50 m radius but inside POL-NS-03's 400 m ceiling, POL-NS-03 still refunds the fee in full; it does not save the charge.

Driver compensation. POL-NS-07 pays only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full; it is not, so there is nothing to pay. The pin-ambiguity goodwill under POL-NS-03(ii) is unavailable because this trip has one registered pickup point and the clause needs two or more — the driver's own concession, which I accept. Under POL-NS-03(i) the residual loss sits with the driver: the rider stated the block in the chat log ('im at blk 118, the one facing the carpark'), the driver read it at 07:22:30 and answered 'ok coming' at 07:22:48, and he never entered the arrival radius before cancelling at 07:33:05. So no compensation is payable, exactly as both sides contend.

On the driver's alternative escalation argument (POL-NS-09(b)): I do not escalate. That limb fires only where two admissible artifacts contradict each other on arrival, dwell or rider presence AND no clause resolves the conflict. A clause resolves it, so limb (b) is not engaged.

Referrals: none. POL-NS-05(ii)'s false-arrival referral is not produced, because the false-marker limb needs a fix at the 'arrived' timestamp more than 300 m out or at 15 km/h or more, and the closest the driver came at any point was 259.94 m — inside the 300 m line — with no distance or speed published for that timestamp. The trip is therefore not recorded as a false-arrival event, as the driver argues.

POL-NS-04: the driver replied to the rider's 07:22:10 message 38 seconds later, so that message was not left unanswered; whether the clause reaches the later unanswered 07:29:15 message does not matter here, because the refund rests on POL-NS-02 and POL-NS-03, which do not depend on POL-NS-04, and the outcome is the same either way.

Integrity and weight. The chat log EV-CHAT-00205 is impaired at weight 0.8 on issue CONTENT_REDACTED; the redaction removed only the unit number and the operative block identifier survives, so the finding built on it stands. The traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00205-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0) and carries no fact; its absence simply means POL-NS-06(i) cannot be run in the driver's favour. No escalation limb is engaged on the profiles: the anti-farming test does not trip (2 no-show terminations against 104 completed trips — below the count of 4 and a rate of 0.019 against 0.08), rider no_show_disputes_30d is 1 against the threshold of 3, and both counterparty-dispute counts are 0. The remaining profile entries — ratings, acceptance rate, lifetime counters — are context only under POL-GEN-01 and ground nothing. Confidence is 0.80: the deciding facts are carried by the GPS trace and the trip record at full weight, and the fault-allocation finding by the chat log at 0.8, whose discount is therefore the cap.

ruling.explanation:
Rider — your dispute succeeds in full and the $4.00 cancellation fee is refunded to you. Driver — the fee cannot stand, and no compensation is payable to you on this record.

WHY THE FEE CANNOT STAND. POL-NS-01 makes a no-show fee chargeable only if all four conditions hold, and two of them fail. Limb (d) fails on the face of the trip record: the trip was terminated by you, the driver, with cancellation_reason_code DRIVER_UNABLE_TO_LOCATE, which POL-NS-01 expressly excludes — it is the driver's own admission that he could not find the rider, and the policy sends such a trip to POL-NS-03. Limb (b) fails as well: of your 92 driver fixes, not one is a qualifying fix inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius, and your closest approach to the Blk 118 pin over the whole trace is 259.94 m. On POL-NS-02 the driver never arrived. POL-NS-06 supplies a second, independent ground: the STANDARD minimum dwell is 300 seconds and the effective in-geofence dwell is 0 seconds (0 qualifying runs, 300-second shortfall), and the advisory you would need in order to have separate intervals summed (EV-ADVIS-00205-01) is MISSING at weight 0.0, so POL-NS-06(i) cannot be run and the shortfall stands.

DRIVER'S COMPENSATION. Both advocates agree the refund follows, and the only live question is your money. POL-NS-03(i) resolves it against you: the rider named the block — 'im at blk 118, the one facing the carpark' at 07:22:10 — you read it at 07:22:30 and answered 'ok coming' at 07:22:48, yet your trace never comes closer than 259.94 m to Blk 118 and you cancelled at 07:33:05 without ever entering the arrival radius. A driver told the correct block, who acknowledges it, and does not move to it before cancelling, bears the loss and receives no compensation. The pin-ambiguity route to a platform-funded goodwill payment (POL-NS-03(ii), 50% = $2.00) is closed because the trip records a single registered pickup point, not two or more.

POL-NS-04. The Rider Advocate's exoneration claim under POL-NS-04 is not reached. Limb (a) is met, but the driver replied to the rider's coordinating message 38 seconds later, and the clause expressly stands down 'where the driver did reply within 120 seconds'. Nothing turns on it, because the full refund and the nil compensation are reached on POL-NS-03 in any event.

ESCALATION. The Driver Advocate's alternative argument under POL-NS-09(b) is rejected. There is no unresolved contradiction: the 'arrived' tap at 07:26:40 is a party-set status, POL-NS-01 measures the wait from GPS entry into the geofence and not from the tap, and POL-NS-03 is the clause the policy provides for exactly this wrong-block situation, with a 400 m ceiling your 259.94 m approach sits inside. No other escalation limb fires either: confidence is 0.8, above the 0.70 floor; the POL-NS-07 anti-farming check fails on both limbs on the only two fields it names (no_show_terminations_30d 2, below 4; rate 0.019, below 0.08); rider no_show_disputes_30d is 1, below 3; and the counterparty-dispute counts are 0 and 0, below 2. POL-GEN-01 bars use of any other profile field, and the driver's rating, acceptance rate and lifetime counters were mentioned only to say they ground nothing.

REFERRALS AND INTEGRITY. On POL-NS-05 the false-arrival marker limb is not made out — the record keys no distance and no speed to the arrived timestamp, and the only published distance (259.94 m) sits inside the 300 m line — so the trip is not recorded as a false-arrival event and no referral issues. POL-NS-08 is not engaged: the arrival timestamp sits within seconds of a GPS fix (no clock skew over 90 s), the trace has no gap over 120 s across its 92 fixes, the chat shows no sequence gap and no 5-minute hole spanning the arrival marker (4 messages against a recorded count of 4), and the $4.00 line reconciles with the fee schedule (STANDARD $4.00 against RYDE_X $4.00, the greater being $4.00).

CONFIDENCE. The chat log EV-CHAT-00205 carries weight 0.8 with issue CONTENT_REDACTED; the redaction removed only the unit number and the operative identifier 'blk 118' survives intact, so the fault finding survives the discount. That 0.8, the lowest weight among the artifacts carrying a deciding fact, caps confidence in this ruling. It is a pre-pass impairment that does not meet the POL-NS-08 limbs, so it down-weights under POL-GEN-02 only and does not compel escalation.

OUTCOME: FULL_REFUND of the $4.00 cancellation fee to the rider; no driver compensation; no referral.

Both counterparts' disputes_with_counterparty_90d are 0. There is no basis to hold this fee away from the rider pending review.

On the remedy: this dispute was filed by the rider, the $4.00 cancellation fee is shown as CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.00, and the amount reconciles with the fee schedule — STANDARD zone fee 4.00 against RYDE_X vehicle tier fee 4.00, the greater of the two being 4.00, so the charge line itself is not in dispute as to quantum. A ruling on POL-NS-01, POL-NS-02, POL-NS-03, POL-NS-04 or POL-NS-06 returns the whole of that $4.00 to the filing party as a FULL_REFUND, with amount_sgd of 4.00.

The rider cannot run this dispute through POL-NS-04, because limb (b) fails on the chat log's own timestamps. Limb (a) is met — the rider's 07:22:10 message names his block — but the driver sent MSG-00205-002 ('ok coming') at 07:22:48, 38 seconds later and far inside the 120 second window, so no finding of unanswered rider contact can be entered against the driver and limb (c) is never reached. Disclosure of impairment, as POL-GEN-02(1) requires: EV-CHAT-00205 carries weight_multiplier 0.8 on issue CONTENT_REDACTED (the unit number in MSG-00205-001 was redacted). The redaction removes no timestamp and no sender, so the 38 second interval this claim rests on is untouched by the discount.

The 4.00 fee cannot be carried by POL-NS-01, and the driver does not pretend otherwise. Limb (d) is excluded by the clause's own text because the trip terminated with cancellation_reason_code DRIVER_UNABLE_TO_LOCATE; limb (b) fails because the driver's nearest approach to the pickup pin is 259.94 m against a 50 m STANDARD arrival radius; and limb (c) fails because the qualifying in-radius fix count is zero out of 92 driver fixes, leaving no in-geofence dwell to set against the 300 second minimum. This is exactly the case POL-NS-01 hands to POL-NS-03 — the category's clause for an honest mislocation rather than a manufactured no-show — and the dispute is to be reasoned there, not on the baseline clause.

What the record does establish is an honest wrong-block attempt, and that distinction should be written into the ruling. The trip record computes a wait_time_min of 6.4 running from the arrived event at 07:26:40 to the cancellation at 07:33:05: the driver gave the rider six and a half minutes rather than harvesting a fee. His closest approach to the pin is 259.94 m — inside POL-NS-03's 400 m wrong-entrance ceiling and inside POL-NS-05's 300 m line. POL-NS-05 catches only an arrival fix that puts the driver more than 300 m out, or in motion at 15 kph or above, at the arrived timestamp; the published derived facts key no distance and no speed to that timestamp, and the only distance they publish sits inside the 300 m line, so the false-marker limb is not made out. This trip therefore belongs to the wrong-entrance route POL-NS-05's closing sentence preserves, and it should not be recorded as a false-arrival event against the driver.

Two points are closed against the driver on this record and the driver does not stretch them. First, the pin-ambiguity limb of POL-NS-03(ii) requires trip_record.registered_pickup_points of 2 or more; this trip records one registered pickup point, so the platform-funded goodwill of 50 per cent — 2.00 against the 4.00 fee — is unavailable and the derived goodwill figure has nothing to attach to. Second, the rider did name the block, MSG-00205-001 reading 'im at blk 118', with the redaction removing only the unit number, so under POL-NS-03(i) the residual loss sits with the driver and no compensation is payable to him. The chat artifact is impaired at weight 0.8 on issue CONTENT_REDACTED, which is why the surviving block identifier, and not the redacted unit number, is the fact relied on.

The sum charged is not open to attack on integrity grounds, and no partial refund can be built on it. The fare breakdown carries a single cancellation-fee line of 4.00 SGD, and 4.00 is exactly the greater of the two schedule figures this trip attracts — the STANDARD zone-class fee of 4.00 and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee of 4.00, the schedule dimension resolving to a tie — so the line reconciles with fee_schedule.resolution_rule and no limb of POL-NS-08(d) is engaged on this trip.

There is no fee-farming pattern behind this cancelled trip. On the two fields POL-NS-07 names, and no others, driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 2, below the 4 the clause requires, and 2 over driver_profile.completed_trips_30d of 104 is a rate of 0.019, below the 0.08 the clause also requires: the anti-farming test fails on both limbs, so nothing on the driver's 30-day record supports an adverse inference. On the rider side, rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 1 against POL-NS-09(d)'s threshold of 3, and the counterparty-dispute counts are 0 and 0 against POL-NS-09(c)'s threshold of 2. Under POL-GEN-01 every other entry on either profile — rating, acceptance rate, lifetime counters — is context only and can ground nothing.

The trip record and the trace contradict each other directly on arrival and dwell: the record enters an arrived event at 07:26:40 with a 6.4 minute wait, while the 92 driver fixes never come closer to the pin than 259.94 m and show zero in-geofence dwell.
